description: E-commerce practice site: browse and search products, add to cart, register an account, place an order.
_VERIFICATION_STATUS: STARTER INVENTORY, NOT YET VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE DOM (31 Jul 2026). The role=, label=, placeholder= and text= selectors are derived from text observed on the real pages, so the names are real - but NONE has been confirmed to resolve to exactly one element. The remaining [data-qa='...'] and #id values are guesses from this site's published test cases and are the most likely to be wrong. Before trusting any of it run `python -m scripts.verify_locators --only-problems` and fix what it reports. Then crawl a fuller draft with `python -m scripts.generate_inventory` and merge in what this file does not cover: the second signup form, product detail, checkout and payment.

_inventory_conventions.selectors: Every selector maps to a first-class Playwright locator: [name='x'] / #id (css), role=button[name='Save'] (getByRole), label=X (getByLabel), placeholder=..., alt=..., title=..., text=... . XPath is never emitted. An iframe-chained selector uses ' >>> '. label=/alt=/title= need page.get_by_label/get_by_alt_text/get_by_title - they are NOT page.locator() engine syntax; role= and text= work with page.locator().
_inventory_conventions.selector_strategy: USER-FACING PLAYWRIGHT LOCATORS FIRST. Ranking, following Playwright's own guidance: test-id > role+accessible-name (getByRole) > label (getByLabel) > aria-label > placeholder > alt > title > stable id / name (css) > nameless role > text > css path. `#id` and `[name=...]` are page.locator() css rather than a getBy* method, so they sit BELOW everything user-facing - they remain above text= and a raw css path, because a deliberate id IS an author's contract, but they are not the first thing to reach for. This app is server-rendered with semantic HTML and readable button and link text, so role= and text= locators fit it especially well.
_inventory_conventions.test_owned_data: An account's cart, addresses and orders are private to it, so assertions on them are safe. The PRODUCT CATALOGUE is shared and read-only - 34 fixed products - so a named product is safe to assert on, but never assert a total that the site owner could change.
_inventory_conventions.icon_only_controls: A control whose visible content is only an icon has NO accessible name, so role=<x>[name='...'] resolves to nothing however sensible the name looks. Prefer role= for anything with readable text; fall back to the id for icon-only buttons. Ranking prefers user-facing locators, but 'user-facing' requires the user to be able to READ something.
_inventory_conventions.icon_ligature_names: Before trusting role=[name='...'], check what the accessible name ACTUALLY is - an icon font that renders from ligature text (Material Icons, some Material Design Web builds) puts that text in the DOM and Playwright includes it in the name. `home Home` is named 'home Home'. Role-name matching is exact, so the obvious selector silently matches nothing. Prefer href for navigation links; verify anything else with verify_locators.
_inventory_conventions.templated_pages: A page that exists once PER RECORD is a template, not an address: store "url": "/product_details/{product_id}" and let the caller supply the id at run time via page_url(product_id=...). Storing a sample id instead would couple every test to whichever record happened to be crawled. Add "url_sample" (e.g. "/product_details/1") so verify_locators and check_inventory_staleness have a real page to check - the elements are identical for every record. Without a sample those tools SKIP the page with a reason rather than navigating to a literal "{product_id}" and reporting every selector as stale.
_inventory_conventions.persistent_state: true when the page shows state the application stores against the signed-in user. Absolute count / emptiness assertions on such a page are rejected at the generation gate unless the scenario establishes the starting state itself.

test_users.registered: A pre-registered account used for login scenarios. No privilege levels exist in this app.

common_errors.invalid_login: Your email or password is incorrect!

elements_notes._shared: Present on every page. Top navigation, so it lives once here rather than repeated on each page.
elements_notes.logout_link: Present ONLY while logged in, which makes its presence a reliable readiness signal for 'am I authenticated'. Use is_visible() on it rather than parsing the URL.
elements_notes.logged_in_as: Reads 'Logged in as <name>'. A substring match, so assert containment rather than equality.
elements_notes.delete_account_link: Permanently removes the account and shows 'ACCOUNT DELETED!'. A test that registers an account should call this at the end - there is no admin cleanup on this site and abandoned accounts accumulate forever.
elements_notes._href_over_role: These are addressed by href, not by role+name, and that is deliberate. This app's nav mixes icon libraries, and Material Icons renders its glyph from LIGATURE TEXT - card_travel puts the literal string 'card_travel' in the DOM. Playwright folds that into the accessible name, so the Products link is named 'card_travel Products', not 'Products', and role=link[name='Products'] matches NOTHING because role-name matching is exact. Links whose icon is Font Awesome (empty ) were unaffected, which is why 'Test Cases' resolved while eight others did not - proven 1 Aug 2026 both against the live site and against reproduced markup. The href is the author's contract and cannot be polluted this way. Each is pinned with '>> nth=0': verified 2 Aug 2026 that the footer repeats Home, Cart, Test Cases and API Testing, so a bare href matched 2-4 elements. The header block precedes the footer in the DOM, so nth=0 is always the header link.
elements_notes.signup_login_link: CONDITIONAL - present only while signed out. Its absence is the same signal as logout_link's presence.

nav.conditional_note: Rendered only while signed OUT — it is replaced by Logout once a session exists. verify_locators signs in before sweeping, so this key always reads STALE there. That is the tool's reach, not a broken selector; the login feature exercises it for real.

elements_notes.subscribe_button: Icon-only button - an arrow glyph, no text - so it has NO accessible name and role=button[name='Subscribe'] matches nothing (verified 1 Aug 2026). The id is the only handle it offers. This is the case where css is genuinely correct.
elements_notes.subscribe_success: Rendered in place after subscribing - there is no navigation and no toast.
elements_notes._naming: No page object exists for this page yet. The subscribe control has no visible label, so name the method for what it does - subscribe_to_newsletter(email) - not a bare subscribe(): the generation gate rejects a bare verb because it does not say what it acts on, and a first attempt that uses one costs a repair call.

elements.login_error: text=Your email or password is incorrect!

elements_notes._two_forms: THIS PAGE CARRIES TWO INDEPENDENT FORMS - 'Login to your account' and 'New User Signup!' - and BOTH have an email field. A selector loose enough to match 'the email input' matches both and is a strict-mode violation. Always use the form-specific key.
elements_notes.login_email_input: UNVERIFIED data-qa value. This app is widely documented as using data-qa attributes, but the exact values here were not read from the DOM. verify_locators will confirm or reject each one in seconds.
elements_notes.signup_button: Submitting this does NOT create the account - it navigates to a second, fuller form at /signup. The account exists only after THAT form is submitted.
elements_notes.login_error: CONDITIONAL - rendered only after a failed login submit. Verified 1 Aug 2026 as absent from a fresh page load, which is correct. Assert on it with the waiting reader (get_login_error); to assert NO error is shown use the non-waiting probe (has_login_error), or the wait will time out instead of returning False.
elements_notes.signup_error: CONDITIONAL - rendered only after submitting the signup form with an email address that already exists. Absent from a fresh page load.
elements_notes._verified: 1 Aug 2026: all 8 unconditional selectors on this page resolve to exactly one element against the live DOM, including every [data-qa='...'] value. The two conditional keys above are unreachable to a tool that cannot click.

errors.invalid_login: Your email or password is incorrect!

login.conditional_note: Elements that exist ONLY after a specific interaction, so they are absent from a freshly loaded page. verify_locators and check_inventory_staleness never click, so they will always report these as STALE - that is the tool being honest about what it cannot reach, NOT a broken selector. Do not 'fix' them on that evidence. They are proven by the E2E suite instead: a scenario that submits bad credentials asserts on login_error.

elements.added_modal: text=Your product has been added to cart.

products.multi_match_note: Keys whose selector matches SEVERAL elements. Read them with get_all_texts / get_count / get_nth_text; to act on ONE member, scope to the row containing its text with click_in_row(); never click, fill or assert on the family as a whole. Enforced by validators/method_resolution_validator.py at generation time.

elements_notes.add_to_cart_buttons: MULTI-MATCH, and worse than it looks: every product card renders its Add to cart control TWICE (once in the card, once in the hover overlay), so this matches 68 elements on the all-products page, not 34. Never click it directly - scope to one product's card, or open the product via its View Product link.
elements_notes.product_names: MULTI-MATCH and also doubled per card for the same reason. Use get_all_texts() to assert a product IS present rather than indexing into it.
elements_notes.view_product_links: MULTI-MATCH - one per product card. Matched by href PREFIX, not by accessible name: role=link[name='View Product'] resolved to ZERO against the live page (2 Aug 2026). The href is exact, carries the product id, and cannot be affected by icon markup inside the link.
elements_notes.added_modal: Adding to cart opens a MODAL rather than navigating. It blocks the page underneath, so a scenario adding two products must dismiss it between them or the second click fails with 'intercepts pointer events'.
elements_notes.search_input: UNVERIFIED id, from the site's documented test cases rather than the DOM. Search matches on product NAME and submits to the same page.
elements_notes._empty_search: A search matching nothing renders NO result cards rather than an empty-state message. Assert absence by counting cards, not by looking for text.
elements_notes.search_button: Icon-only button (magnifier glyph), no accessible name - same as home.subscribe_button. css id is the right locator here.
elements_notes.searched_products_heading: Replaces the All Products heading once a search has actually run - a term was entered and submitted. This is the only reliable signal that the search EXECUTED: a result count alone cannot tell 'the search returned one product' from 'the search never ran and the page still shows the full catalogue'. It does NOT appear for an empty query; see all_products_heading.
elements_notes.all_products_heading: Shown on the unsearched listing. Its DISAPPEARANCE is the mirror signal to searched_products_heading. AN EMPTY SEARCH DOES NOT RUN A SEARCH: submitting the form with no term leaves this heading in place and shows the full catalogue, so a scenario about an empty query must assert THIS heading, never searched_products_heading. Measured 15 Sep 2026: text=Searched Products matches 0 on /products?search=.
elements_notes.continue_shopping_button: INSIDE the add-to-cart modal, so a product must be added before it exists. Use it to dismiss the modal and stay on the listing - a scenario adding a SECOND product must click this first, or the next click lands on the overlay rather than the page.
elements_notes.view_cart_link_in_modal: INSIDE the add-to-cart modal. The other way out of it: navigates to the cart instead of dismissing. Prefer this over the nav Cart link when a scenario has just added a product, because it also proves the modal appeared.
elements_notes.product_cards: MULTI-MATCH, one per card. NOT doubled - unlike product_names and add_to_cart_buttons, which render twice per card. Never take an index from a doubled family and apply it to this one: use click_in_row() to scope to the card containing the product name instead.

products.conditional_note: None of these exist on a freshly loaded page, so a tool that only navigates always reads them as absent - that is its reach, not a broken selector. added_modal, continue_shopping_button and view_cart_link_in_modal appear only after a product is added to the cart. searched_products_heading appears only after a search has run.

cart.multi_match_note: Keys whose selector matches SEVERAL elements. Read them with get_all_texts / get_count / get_nth_text; to act on ONE member, scope to the row containing its text with click_in_row(); never click, fill or assert on the family as a whole.

elements_notes._test_owned: The cart belongs to this test's own session or account, so asserting an EXACT row count is safe here - unlike the shared catalogue.
elements_notes.cart_rows: MULTI-MATCH. Narrow to the product the test added rather than assuming a row index.
elements_notes.cart_table: UNVERIFIED id, from the site's documented test cases rather than the DOM.
elements_notes.proceed_to_checkout_button: Matched by TEXT. role=link[name='Proceed To Checkout'] resolved to zero (2 Aug 2026) - the control is an anchor without an href, so it carries no link role. Proceeding while signed out shows a Register/Login prompt instead of the address form.
elements_notes.empty_cart_message: Rendered ONLY when the cart holds nothing - the mirror of cart_rows, and exactly one of the two is present at any moment. Asserting on it means asserting the cart is empty ABSOLUTELY, so the scenario must have started from a known state: see _starting_state.
elements_notes._starting_state: The cart PERSISTS for a registered account across logout and across runs. Private to the account is not the same as empty: a run that added an item and failed before removing it leaves that item behind, so the next run finds one more than it put there - and a scenario asserting the cart is EMPTY after its own removal still sees the leftover. A scenario asserting an absolute state must own its starting state: register a fresh account with the unique_username fixture, or empty the cart first. Otherwise assert relatively - that the product this test added is present - which is true whatever the account started with.

cart.conditional_note: Only rendered when the cart is empty, so it reads STALE whenever the sweep runs against a cart with items in it.
cart.persistent_state_note: The cart is stored against the signed-in account. It survives logout and survives the run, so a scenario reusing a shared account inherits whatever a previous run left behind. A scenario asserting an ABSOLUTE count or emptiness here must first own its starting state: register a fresh account, or clear the state explicitly.

notes.cart_quantities: The quantity cell, RELATIVE to a cart row. get_column_values() and get_cell_text() scope this selector INSIDE the row, so an absolute form like '#cart_info .cart_quantity' matches nothing - the id is an ancestor of the row, not a descendant. Read one row's value with get_column_values(cart_rows, cart_quantities, 0) plus find_row_index_by_text(cart_rows, <product name>).
notes.row_family: The repeating CONTAINER. Reading its text gives every cell of a row concatenated, which is what the reader-naming rule exists to catch. The other families here are columns of single fields - reading their text with get_all_texts() is correct and must not be flagged.
notes.conditional: Two opposite states, both legitimate. `empty_cart_message` exists ONLY while the cart is empty; the row-dependent keys exist ONLY while it is not. Whichever state the browser is in, the other list reads as zero matches - so both are declared conditional and the verifier reports COND rather than STALE. Declaring only one side is what turned an empty cart into five drift findings.

product_detail.conditional_note: The add-to-cart modal does not exist until Add to cart is clicked, and review_success not until a review is submitted. A tool that only navigates always reads these as absent - that is its reach, not a broken selector.

elements_notes._url: TEMPLATE, not an address: one page per product. Open it with page_url(product_id=...), or better, reach it by clicking a product's View Product link on the listing - that href already carries the id, so the test never invents one.
elements_notes.add_to_cart_button: The single add-to-cart control for THIS product. Unlike the listing page's family of 68, this one is unique - which is why a cart scenario should add a product from here rather than from the listing.
elements_notes.quantity_input: Type a quantity BEFORE adding to cart; changing it afterwards does not update the cart.
elements_notes.added_modal: Adding to cart opens a MODAL rather than navigating, and it blocks the page underneath. A scenario adding two products must dismiss it between them or the second click lands on the overlay.
elements_notes.product_price: Rendered as 'Rs. 500'. Assert on the number, not the format.
elements_notes._naming: No page object exists for this page yet. Agent 2 chooses its method names, guided by the naming rule in the generation prompt: a bare verb such as open() or submit() collides with the first specific method that shares it, so a method must say WHAT it acts on - open_product(), not open(). Every later story reads the real signatures back from the file, so the names are chosen once. Do not fill key_methods back in.
elements_notes.view_cart_link_in_modal: INSIDE the add-to-cart modal, which appears only after Add to cart is clicked on this page. Navigates to the cart.
elements_notes.continue_shopping_button: INSIDE the add-to-cart modal. Dismisses it and stays on this product. Needed before any further interaction with the page underneath, because the modal blocks it.
elements_notes.review_success: Appears only after a review is submitted successfully. A review needs a name, an email and review text; submitting an incomplete form is blocked by the browser's own validation, so nothing app-authored appears and this element never renders.

_starting_state.note: How a scenario can honestly own its starting state in THIS application. Both lists are EMPTY on purpose: registration needs a second form this inventory does not describe, and the cart is cleared by hand before a run rather than by generated steps. So the only remedy this application offers is a RELATIVE assertion - that what the scenario added is present, or is gone - which needs one file and no coordination.
